skill.name: code-consistency-validator
skill.description: Validates type consistency across Rust, TypeScript, and PostgreSQL boundaries. Useful for code review, mismatch debugging, and API contract validation.
skill.summary: Checks cross-language type consistency across Rust, TypeScript, and PostgreSQL code paths.
skill.author: BarisSozen

security_audit.summary: The three static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, not executable Ruby backtick shell calls. SKILL.md includes benign grep examples for local review and no evidence of prompt injection or data exfiltration.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 43 starts a Markdown TypeScript code fence for example type-conversion patterns. It is not Ruby backtick execution and does not invoke a shell.
Line 47 is the closing Markdown code fence for the TypeScript examples. There is no command execution primitive or user-controlled shell input.
Line 50 starts a Markdown bash example with read-only grep commands for local review. It is not automatic shell execution and contains no interpolation or exfiltration behavior.

content.value_statement: Cross-language type drift can cause precision loss and contract bugs. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Rust, TypeScript, and PostgreSQL checks.
actual_capabilities: Reviews Rust, TypeScript, and PostgreSQL type mappings for consistency.
Highlights precision risks around wei, balances, amounts, and BigInt values.
Checks TypeScript parseInt usage for missing radix arguments.
Flags unsafe BigInt serialization patterns in API payloads.
Provides grep-based search patterns for targeted local review.
Formats results with critical, warning, info, and validated outcomes.
limitations: It does not run tests or prove runtime behavior by itself.
It focuses on Rust, TypeScript, and PostgreSQL boundaries.
Grep patterns can miss aliases, generated files, or indirect conversions.
It supplements compiler checks, schema reviews, and migration tests.

use_cases.title: Review Financial Type Safety
use_cases.description: Check balance, amount, and wei handling before shipping payment or blockchain code.

use_cases.title: Validate API Contracts
use_cases.description: Compare Rust models, TypeScript clients, and PostgreSQL schemas for mismatched numeric types.

use_cases.title: Audit Database Migrations
use_cases.description: Inspect schema changes for type choices that can truncate, round, or overflow values.

prompt_templates.title: Check Basic Type Mappings
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this change for Rust, TypeScript, and PostgreSQL type consistency. Focus on obvious mismatches and summarize risks by severity.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small pull request

prompt_templates.title: Find Precision Loss Risks
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this code for numeric precision risks around balances, amounts, wei values, BigInt, and parseInt usage.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of financial or blockchain logic

prompt_templates.title: Validate API Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the API contract across server models, client types, and database columns. Identify any unsafe conversions or serialization issues.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of cross-service data flow

prompt_templates.title: Produce Release Gate Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the changed files for cross-language type consistency and produce a release gate report with critical, warning, info, and validated items.

output_examples.input: Review TypeScript balance handling for wei values.
output_examples.output: Critical: A wei balance is converted to a floating point number. Keep the value as bigint or string across the API boundary.

output_examples.input: Check a Rust amount field against a PostgreSQL migration.
output_examples.output: Warning: The application uses an unsigned 64-bit value, but the database column may not preserve the full expected range.

output_examples.input: Validate a pull request that changes parseInt calls.
output_examples.output: Info: Add an explicit radix where decimal or hexadecimal intent matters. No direct precision-loss path was confirmed.

best_practices: Review type definitions, serialization, and database columns together.
Treat financial and blockchain amounts as exact values, not floating point numbers.
Confirm warnings with compiler checks, tests, and migration validation.
anti_patterns: Do not convert large integer balances to ordinary numbers.
Do not assume client types match server or database types automatically.
Do not rely only on grep results for final release approval.

faq.question: What languages does this skill focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on Rust, TypeScript, and PostgreSQL type boundaries.

faq.question: Can it find precision loss bugs?
faq.answer: It can guide searches for common precision loss patterns, especially around balances, amounts, wei values, and BigInt.

faq.question: Does it execute code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides review guidance and example grep commands for local inspection.

faq.question: Is this a replacement for tests?
faq.answer: No. Use it with unit tests, integration tests, compiler checks, and migration validation.

faq.question: Can Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should reviewers prioritize first?
faq.answer: Start with money-like values, API payloads, BigInt serialization, and database columns that store large numeric values.
